title: Juntos Unidos, Now and Next

body_markdown:
By **Kristy Williams**


November 13, 2026 02:11 PM Eastern Daylight Time


> *As leaders pass the torch within the Juntos Unidos Employee Business Resource Group, outgoing and incoming co-leads reflect on what’s been built and share what’s coming next.*


Throughout Hispanic Heritage Month, Juntos Unidos hosted a month of events and celebration, including a speaker session with radio personality and journalist Honey German.


Moments like this are part of why Juntos Unidos was created: to bring together employees from across the business to celebrate their culture and their peers.


The employee business resource group (EBRG) spans corporate offices, retail stores, distribution centers, and workshops, led by Diana Costescu, Director, Talent Acquisition, and Yolanda Ramos-Giraldo, Manager, Global Mobility. However, after two years at the helm they will transition leadership to Viviana Narvaez, Senior Manager, Digital Engineering, and Patricia Ramirez, Manager, Asset Project Management, as part of a leadership rotation that all Tapestry’s EBRGs follow.


“I think employees don’t realize how much work it goes into launching and running an employee resource group,” says Ramos-Giraldo. “I think they see activations, but they don’t see us standing and trying to plan stuff that’s impactful.”


So, we sat down with the four leaders to discuss what it takes to run Juntos Unidos, the group’s accomplishments, and what they’re looking forward to next.


**What They’ve Built**


“I’m really proud of the recognition that we’ve given to our colleagues in the workshop, distribution centers, and just bringing them into our community as much as we can,” says Costescu. “They get to step away from their work and really honor their heritage and be honored.”


Ramos-Giraldo points to the mixers Juntos Unidos has hosted to get to know one another better. “We always make sure there’s a game,” she says. “People are having a good time, people are meeting other people, and they’re getting that sense of community.”


To connect with colleagues who operate on different schedules, Juntos Unidos offers ways to connect and community-build outside of working hours. The group hosts a book club, where participants discuss titles by Latinx authors, while other members took Spanish Duolingo lessons together.


**Skill-Building to Lead**


EBRG involvement is also a way to build skills. “You’ll definitely stretch as a member of an EBRG and have to work with others and really collaborate and plan your time and delegate and execute,” Costescu says. Incoming co-lead Ramirez says it has widened her circle: “I’ve met so many people that I would have never otherwise in so many different parts of the business.”


Juntos also offered Ramirez a space to become comfortable with public speaking and come out of her shell. “EBRGs give our co-leads and pillar leads an opportunity to stretch in a very different way. We’re all figuring it out together,” says Costescu.


**What’s Next**


The incoming co-leads say they’re building on what Costescu and Ramos-Giraldo have built. “Diana and Yolanda have done great work the past two years,” says Ramirez.


Narvaez is looking forward to including more countries in the group’s events and activities. “We come in every shape, shade and color, and we have such a diverse culture we can bring to light,” she says.


“I hope I can make a bigger impact,” says Narvaez. “I have a lot of ideas.”


Ramirez wants to meet co-leads from other EBRGs and plan more collaborative events. As a project manager, organization is top of mind, but she’s also thinking about program expansion and how to find people who understand what community-building really means.


“Finding the right ways to communicate all together, it’s not easy because everybody has such different job functions,” says Ramirez. “But \[it’s about\] making sure they feel supported while also being able to bring in more people who are like willing to help or understand what we’re doing and who we are.”


For anyone interested in joining an EBRG, Ramirez says membership is flexible. “Membership doesn’t require anything other than, you see our notifications. When you want to join, you join.”
